title_en: Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purpose of safeguarding cybersecurity, maintaining cyberspace sovereignty and national security and social public interests, protecting the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons and other organizations, and promoting the healthy development of economic and social informatization.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to the construction, operation, maintenance and use of networks within the territory of the People's Republic of China, as well as the supervision and administration of cybersecurity.

Article 3 Cybersecurity work shall adhere to the leadership of the Communist Party of China, implement the holistic approach to national security, coordinate development and security, and promote the building of a cyber power.

Article 4 The State shall adhere to the principle of equal emphasis on cybersecurity and informatization development, follow the policy of active use, scientific development, lawful governance, and ensuring security, promote the construction and interconnection of network infrastructure, encourage technological innovation and application of networks, support the cultivation of cybersecurity talents, establish and improve the cybersecurity assurance system, and enhance cybersecurity protection capabilities.

Article 5 The State shall formulate and continuously improve the cybersecurity strategy, define the basic requirements and main objectives for ensuring cybersecurity, and propose cybersecurity policies, work tasks and measures in key areas.

Article 6 The State shall take measures to monitor, prevent and handle cybersecurity risks and threats from inside and outside the territory of the People's Republic of China, protect critical information infrastructure from attacks, intrusions, interference and destruction, punish cybercrimes and illegal activities according to law, and maintain cyberspace security and order.

Article 7 The State shall advocate honest, trustworthy, healthy and civilized online behavior, promote the dissemination of socialist core values, take measures to improve the cybersecurity awareness and level of the whole society, and form a favorable environment in which the whole society jointly participates in promoting cybersecurity.

Article 8 The State shall actively engage in international exchanges and cooperation in cyberspace governance, research and development of network technologies and standard setting, and combating cybercrimes and other illegal activities, so as to promote the building of a peaceful, secure, open and cooperative cyberspace and the establishment of a multilateral, democratic and transparent cyberspace governance system.

Article 9 The national cyberspace administration shall be responsible for coordinating cybersecurity work and relevant supervision and administration. The telecommunications authority, public security authority and other relevant authorities under the State Council shall, in accordance with the provisions of this Law and relevant laws and administrative regulations, be responsible for cybersecurity protection and supervision and administration within the scope of their respective duties.
The duties of the relevant departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level concerning cybersecurity protection and supervision and administration shall be determined in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 10 Network operators must, in carrying out their business and service activities, comply with laws and administrative regulations, respect social morality, observe business ethics, act in good faith, fulfill cybersecurity protection obligations, accept supervision from the government and the public, and bear social responsibilities.

Article 11 Construction, operation of networks or provision of services through networks shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations and the mandatory requirements of national standards, adopt technical measures and other necessary measures to ensure the secure and stable operation of networks, effectively respond to cybersecurity incidents, prevent cybercrimes and other illegal activities, and maintain the integrity, confidentiality and availability of network data.

Article 12 Relevant industry organizations of networks shall, in accordance with their articles of association, strengthen industry self-discipline, formulate cybersecurity behavior norms, guide their members to strengthen cybersecurity protection, improve the level of cybersecurity protection, and promote the healthy development of the industry.

Article 13 The State shall protect the right of citizens, legal persons and other organizations to use networks according to law, promote universal access to networks, improve the level of network services, provide safe and convenient network services for the society, and ensure the orderly and free flow of network information according to law.
Any individual or organization using networks shall comply with the Constitution and laws, adhere to public order, respect social morality, and shall not endanger cybersecurity, nor use networks to engage in activities endangering national security, honor and interests, inciting subversion of state power, overthrowing the socialist system, inciting secession, undermining national unity, promoting terrorism and extremism, promoting ethnic hatred and discrimination, disseminating violence, obscenity or pornography, fabricating or disseminating false information to disrupt economic order and social order, or infringing upon the reputation, privacy, intellectual property rights and other lawful rights and interests of others.

Article 14 The State shall support the research and development of network products and services that are conducive to the healthy growth of minors, punish according to law activities that use networks to harm the physical and mental health of minors, and provide a safe and healthy network environment for minors.

Article 15 Any individual or organization shall have the right to report acts that endanger cybersecurity to the cyberspace administration, telecommunications authority, public security authority and other departments. The department that receives the report shall timely handle it according to law; if it is not within the scope of its duties, it shall promptly transfer the report to the department with authority to handle it.
The relevant department shall keep confidential the relevant information of the informant and protect the lawful rights and interests of the informant.

Article 16 The State shall establish and improve the cybersecurity standard system. The standardization administrative department under the State Council and other relevant departments under the State Council shall, in accordance with their respective duties, organize the formulation and timely revision of national standards and industry standards concerning network security management and the security of network products, services and operations.
The State shall support enterprises, research institutions, institutions of higher learning, and relevant industry organizations of networks to participate in the formulation of national standards and industry standards for cybersecurity.

Article 17 The State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall make overall plans, increase investment, support key cybersecurity technology industries and projects, support the research, development and application of cybersecurity technologies, promote secure and trustworthy network products and services, protect intellectual property rights in network technologies, and support enterprises, research institutions, institutions of higher learning and other entities to participate in national cybersecurity technology innovation projects.

Article 18 The State shall promote the construction of a socialized service system for cybersecurity, and encourage relevant enterprises and institutions to carry out security services such as cybersecurity certification, testing and risk assessment.

Article 19 The State shall encourage the development of technologies for the protection and utilization of network data security, promote the opening of public data resources, and drive technological innovation and economic and social development.

Article 20 The State shall support the research and development of key technologies such as basic theory research and algorithms of artificial intelligence, promote the construction of infrastructure such as training data resources and computing power, improve ethical norms for artificial intelligence, strengthen risk monitoring, assessment and safety supervision, and promote the application and healthy development of artificial intelligence.
The State shall support innovative approaches to network security management, and use new technologies such as artificial intelligence to enhance the level of cybersecurity protection.

Article 21 The people's governments at all levels and the relevant departments thereof shall organize regular publicity and education on cybersecurity, and shall guide and supervise relevant entities in conducting such publicity and education.
The mass media shall conduct targeted cybersecurity publicity and education for the public.

Article 22 The State shall support enterprises, institutions of higher education, vocational schools, and other education and training institutions in carrying out education and training on cybersecurity, and in cultivating cybersecurity talents through various means, and shall promote the exchange of cybersecurity talents.

Article 42 A network operator shall keep strictly confidential the user information it collects and shall establish and improve a user information protection system.
When processing personal information, a network operator shall comply with the provisions of this Law, the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, and other laws and administrative regulations.

Article 43 A network operator, when collecting and using personal information, shall follow the principles of lawfulness, propriety, and necessity, shall disclose the rules for collection and use, shall clearly indicate the purpose, method, and scope of collection and use of information, and shall obtain the consent of the person from whom the information is collected.
A network operator shall not collect personal information unrelated to the services it provides, shall not collect or use personal information in violation of the provisions of laws and administrative regulations or the agreement between the parties, and shall process the personal information it retains in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations and its agreement with the user.

Article 44 A network operator shall not disclose, tamper with, or destroy the personal information it collects; without the consent of the person from whom the information is collected, it shall not provide personal information to others. This shall not apply to information that has been processed in such a way that no specific individual can be identified and cannot be restored.
A network operator shall adopt technical measures and other necessary measures to ensure the security of the personal information it collects and to prevent the disclosure, destruction, or loss of such information. Where a disclosure, destruction, or loss of personal information occurs or may occur, it shall immediately take remedial measures, promptly inform the users in accordance with the provisions, and report to the relevant competent departments.

Article 45 Where an individual discovers that a network operator collects or uses his personal information in violation of the provisions of laws or administrative regulations or the agreement between the parties, he shall have the right to demand that the network operator delete his personal information; where he discovers that his personal information collected and stored by the network operator contains errors, he shall have the right to demand that the network operator make corrections. The network operator shall take measures to delete or correct the information.
Article 46 No individual or organization may steal or otherwise illegally obtain personal information, or illegally sell or illegally provide personal information to others.

Article 47 The departments and their staff members that are responsible for cybersecurity supervision and administration according to law must strictly keep confidential the personal information, privacy, and trade secrets known to them in the performance of their duties, and shall not disclose, sell, or illegally provide such information to others.

Article 48 Any individual or organization shall be responsible for the acts of using the network, and shall not set up websites or communication groups used to commit fraud, teach criminal methods, produce or sell prohibited or controlled articles, or other illegal and criminal activities, and shall not use the network to publish information involved in committing fraud, producing or selling prohibited or controlled articles, or other illegal and criminal activities.

Article 49 A network operator shall strengthen the management of information published by its users. Where it discovers information the publication or transmission of which is prohibited by laws or administrative regulations, it shall immediately stop transmitting such information, take measures such as eliminating the information to prevent its dissemination, preserve relevant records, and report to the relevant competent departments.

Article 50 The electronic information sent or the application software provided by any individual or organization shall not contain malicious programs, and shall not contain information the publication or transmission of which is prohibited by laws or administrative regulations.
Electronic information sending service providers and application software download service providers shall perform security management obligations. Where they know that their users have engaged in the conduct specified in the preceding paragraph, they shall stop providing services, take measures such as eliminating the information, preserve relevant records, and report to the relevant competent departments.

Article 51 A network operator shall establish a system for complaints and reports on cybersecurity information, publish information such as the methods for complaints and reports, and timely accept and handle complaints and reports on cybersecurity information.
A network operator shall cooperate with the cyberspace administration department and other relevant departments in the supervision and inspection conducted according to law.

Article 52 The national cyberspace administration department and other relevant departments shall perform their duties of cybersecurity information supervision and administration according to law. Where they discover information the publication or transmission of which is prohibited by laws or administrative regulations, they shall require the network operator to stop transmission, take measures such as eliminating the information, and preserve relevant records; with respect to the aforesaid information originating from outside the territory of the People's Republic of China, they shall notify the relevant institutions to take technical measures and other necessary measures to block its dissemination.

Article 53 The State shall establish a system for cybersecurity monitoring, early warning, and information notification. The national cyberspace administration department shall coordinate with other relevant departments to strengthen the collection, analysis, and notification of cybersecurity information, and shall uniformly publish cybersecurity monitoring and early warning information in accordance with the provisions.

Article 54 The departments responsible for the security protection of critical information infrastructure shall establish and improve the cybersecurity monitoring, early warning, and information notification systems for their respective industries and fields, and shall submit cybersecurity monitoring and early warning information in accordance with the provisions.

Article 55 The national cyberspace administration department shall coordinate with other relevant departments to establish and improve a cybersecurity risk assessment and emergency response mechanism, formulate a cybersecurity incident emergency plan, and organize drills on a regular basis.
The departments responsible for the security protection of critical information infrastructure shall formulate cybersecurity incident emergency plans for their respective industries and fields, and organize drills on a regular basis.
The cybersecurity incident emergency plan shall classify cybersecurity incidents according to factors such as the degree of harm and scope of impact after the incident occurs, and shall stipulate corresponding emergency response measures.

Article 57 Where a cybersecurity incident occurs, the cybersecurity incident emergency plan shall be immediately activated, the cybersecurity incident shall be investigated and assessed, and the network operator shall be required to take technical measures and other necessary measures to eliminate security risks, prevent the expansion of harm, and timely issue warning information relevant to the public.

Article 58 Where, in the course of performing their cybersecurity supervision and administration duties, the relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level discover that a network has a relatively large security risk or has experienced a security incident, they may, in accordance with the prescribed authority and procedures, admonish the legal representative or principal person in charge of the network operator. The network operator shall, as required, take measures to make corrections and eliminate the hazards.

Article 59 Where an emergency or a production safety accident occurs as a result of a cybersecurity incident, it shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the Emergency Response Law of the People's Republic of China, the Production Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 60 Where necessary for maintaining national security and public social order and dealing with major sudden social security incidents, upon decision or approval of the State Council, provisional measures such as restrictions on network communications may be taken in a specific area.

Article 61 Where a network operator fails to perform the cybersecurity protection obligations prescribed in Articles 23 and 27 of this Law, the relevant competent department shall order it to make corrections, give it a warning, and may impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan; if it refuses to make corrections or causes consequences such as endangering cybersecurity, a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed, and a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed on the directly responsible的主管和其他直接责任人员.\nWhere an operator of critical information infrastructure fails to perform the cybersecurity protection obligations prescribed in Articles 35, 36, 38, and 40 of this Law, the relevant competent department shall order it to make corrections, give it a warning, and may impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan; if it refuses to make corrections or causes consequences such as endangering cybersecurity, a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed, and a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed on the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons.\nWhere the conduct in the preceding two paragraphs causes serious consequences endangering cybersecurity, such as massive data leakage or partial loss of function of critical information infrastructure, the relevant competent department shall impose a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 2,000,000 yuan, and a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan on the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons; where it causes especially serious consequences endangering cybersecurity, such as loss of main functions of critical information infrastructure, a fine of not less than 2,000,000 yuan but not more than 10,000,000 yuan shall be imposed, and a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan on the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons.

Article 63 Where, in violation of Article 25 of this Law, network critical equipment or specialized cybersecurity products that have not undergone security certification or security testing, or that fail to pass security certification or do not meet the requirements of security testing are sold or provided, the relevant competent department shall order the cessation of the sale or provision, give a warning, and confiscate the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 100,000 yuan, a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall also be imposed; if the illegal gains are 100,000 yuan or more, a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains shall also be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, it may also order the suspension of relevant business, rectification for suspension of business, revocation of the relevant business license, or revocation of the business license. Where other laws or administrative regulations provide otherwise, those provisions shall prevail.

Article 64 Where a network operator, in violation of Article 26, paragraph 1 of this Law, fails to require users to provide true identity information, or provides relevant services to users who do not provide true identity information, the relevant competent department shall order it to make corrections; if it refuses to make corrections or the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed, and it may order the suspension of relevant business, rectification for suspension of business, closure of the website or application, revocation of the relevant business license, or revocation of the business license, and a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed on the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons.

Article 65 Where, in violation of Article 28 of this Law, activities such as cybersecurity certification, testing, or risk assessment are conducted, or cybersecurity information such as system vulnerabilities, computer viruses, network attacks, or network intrusions is released to the public, the relevant competent department shall order corrections and give a warning, and may impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan; if it refuses to make corrections or the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed, and it may order the suspension of relevant business, rectification for suspension of business, closure of the website or application, revocation of the relevant business license, or revocation of the business license, and a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed on the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons.\nWhere the conduct in the preceding paragraph causes the consequences specified in Article 61, paragraph 3 of this Law, punishment shall be imposed in accordance with that paragraph.

Article 66 Where, in violation of Article 29 of this Law, anyone engages in activities endangering cybersecurity, or provides programs or tools specifically used for engaging in activities endangering cybersecurity, or provides assistance such as technical support, advertising promotion, or payment settlement to others for engaging in activities endangering cybersecurity, which is not serious enough to constitute a crime, the public security organ shall confiscate the illegal gains, impose detention of not more than five days, and may concurrently impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan; if the circumstances are relatively serious, detention of not less than five days but not more than fifteen days shall be imposed, and a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan may concurrently be imposed.\nWhere a unit commits the conduct in the preceding paragraph, the public security organ shall confiscate the illegal gains, impose a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan, and shall punish the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons in accordance with the preceding paragraph.\nA person who, in violation of Article 29 of this Law, has been subjected to public security administration punishment shall not engage in work in key positions of cybersecurity management or network operation within five years; a person who has been subjected to criminal punishment shall not engage in work in key positions of cybersecurity management or network operation for life.

Article 67 Where an operator of critical information infrastructure, in violation of Article 37 of this Law, uses network products or services that have not undergone security review or have not passed security review, the relevant competent department shall order it to make corrections within a time limit, cease the use, eliminate the impact on national security, and impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than ten times the procurement amount, and a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed on the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons.

Article 68 Where, in violation of Article 48 of this Law, a website or communication group used for committing illegal or criminal activities is established, or information involving the commission of illegal or criminal activities is published through the network, which is not serious enough to constitute a crime, the public security organ shall impose detention of not more than five days, and may concurrently impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan; if the circumstances are relatively serious, detention of not less than five days but not more than fifteen days shall be imposed, and a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan may concurrently be imposed. The website or communication group used for committing illegal or criminal activities shall be closed.\nWhere a unit commits the conduct in the preceding paragraph, the public security organ shall impose a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan, and shall punish the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 69 Where a network operator, in violation of Article 49 of this Law, fails to stop the transmission of information prohibited from being published or transmitted by laws or administrative regulations, or fails to take disposal measures such as elimination, or fails to preserve relevant records, or fails to report to the relevant competent department, or in violation of Article 52 of this Law, fails to stop the transmission of information prohibited from being published or transmitted by laws or administrative regulations in accordance with the requirements of the relevant department, or fails to take disposal measures such as elimination, or fails to preserve relevant records, the relevant competent department shall order corrections, give a warning, and circulate a notice, and may impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan; if it refuses to make corrections or the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 2,000,000 yuan shall be imposed, and it may order the suspension of relevant business, rectification for suspension of business, closure of the website or application, revocation of the relevant business license, or revocation of the business license, and a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan shall be imposed on the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons.\nWhere the conduct in the preceding paragraph causes especially serious impact or especially serious consequences, the relevant competent department shall impose a fine of not less than 2,000,000 yuan but not more than 10,000,000 yuan, order the suspension of relevant business, rectification for suspension of business, closure of the website or application, revocation of the relevant business license, or revocation of the business license, and impose a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan on the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons.\nWhere an electronic information transmission service provider or an application software download service provider fails to perform the security management obligations prescribed in Article 50, paragraph 2 of this Law, it shall be punished in accordance with the preceding two paragraphs.

Article 70 Where a network operator violates the provisions of this Law and commits any of the following acts, the relevant competent department shall order it to make corrections; if it refuses to make corrections or the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed, and a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed on the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons:\n(1) refusing or obstructing the supervision and inspection lawfully conducted by the relevant department;\n(2) refusing to provide technical support and assistance to the public security organ or the national security organ.

Article 72 Where there is an illegal act provided for in this Law, it shall be recorded in the credit file in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations, and shall be publicized.

Article 73 Where the provisions of this Law are violated, but there are circumstances for a lighter, mitigated, or no punishment as prescribed in the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China, a lighter, mitigated, or no punishment shall be imposed in accordance with its provisions.

Article 74 Where an operator of a government affairs network of a state organ fails to perform the cybersecurity protection obligations prescribed in this Law, its superior organ or the relevant organ shall order it to make corrections; the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 75 Where the cyberspace administration department and relevant departments, in violation of Article 32 of this Law, use the information obtained in the performance of their cybersecurity protection duties for other purposes, the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions according to law.\nWhere a staff member of the cyberspace administration department or relevant department neglects duties, abuses power, or engages in favoritism and malpractice, which is not serious enough to constitute a crime, he or she shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 76 Where the provisions of this Law are violated, causing damage to others, civil liability shall be borne according to law.\nWhere the provisions of this Law are violated, constituting a violation of public security administration, public security administration punishment shall be imposed according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 77 Where an overseas institution, organization, or individual engages in activities endangering the cybersecurity of the People's Republic of China, legal liability shall be investigated according to law; if serious consequences are caused, the public security department of the State Council and relevant departments may also decide to take measures such as freezing property or other necessary sanctions against such institution, organization, or individual.

Article 78 For the purposes of this Law, the following terms shall have the meanings assigned to them:
(1) "Network" means a system composed of computers or other information terminals and related equipment, which collects, stores, transmits, exchanges, and processes information in accordance with certain rules and procedures.
(2) "Cybersecurity" means the ability to prevent attacks, intrusions, interference, destruction, and unlawful use of the network, as well as unexpected accidents, through the adoption of necessary measures, so that the network is in a state of stable and reliable operation, and to ensure the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of network data.
(3) "Network operator" means the owner, manager, and network service provider of a network.
(4) "Network data" means various electronic data collected, stored, transmitted, processed, and generated through the network.
(5) "Personal information" means all kinds of information recorded electronically or by other means, which can be used alone or in combination with other information to identify the identity of a natural person, including but not limited to the natural person's name, date of birth, identity document number, personal biometric information, address, telephone number, etc.

Article 79 The protection of the operational security of networks that store or process information involving state secrets shall, in addition to complying with this Law, also comply with the provisions of secrecy-related laws and administrative regulations.
Article 80 The security protection of military networks shall be separately prescribed by the Central Military Commission.
Article 81 This Law shall come into force from June 1, 2017.
